title: algorithm
short_summary: The English word “algorithm” ultimately comes from the Latinized name of the Persian mathematician Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī. It first referred to arithmetic using Hindu-Arabic numerals and later broadened to mean a step-by-step computational procedure.
confidence_summary: The connection to al-Khwārizmī’s Latinized name is well established. The simplified route through Medieval Latin and later European mathematical vocabulary is sufficient for prototype purposes.

forms.meaning: a step-by-step procedure for calculation, problem-solving, or computation

edges.note: Modern algorithm is historically related to earlier English algorism/algorisme, with later spelling influenced by Greek-looking forms such as arithmetic.
Middle English algorisme was borrowed from Old French/Medieval Latin mathematical vocabulary; this prototype simplifies the route through Medieval Latin.
Medieval Latin algorismus comes from the Latinized name of al-Khwārizmī.
The name al-Khwārizmī indicates association with Khwarazm.

semantic_stages.label: Personal name
semantic_stages.meaning: Al-Khwārizmī was the name by which the Persian mathematician Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī was known in Arabic scholarly tradition.

semantic_stages.label: Arithmetic with Hindu-Arabic numerals
semantic_stages.meaning: Medieval Latin algorismus referred to calculation methods associated with Hindu-Arabic numerals.

semantic_stages.label: Step-by-step procedure
semantic_stages.meaning: In modern usage, algorithm means a general step-by-step procedure for solving a problem or performing computation.

historical_context: Algorithm is especially useful for the project because it is not simply a loanword chain. It shows how a personal name became a technical term, first for numerical calculation and later for computation in general.
